mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the decision date is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financing conditions for corporate investment and consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the prior month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-tightening period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs in the prior month coincides with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days, reflecting optimism about labor market resilience and corporate hiring momentum.
failure_condition: In regimes with high inflation, the 60-day forward return is not statistically superior to a neutral benchmark (mean of prior 30-day returns).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 index points in the prior month predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days, as weak manufacturing momentum signals impending market repricing of economic weakness.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 100 index in the prior month
regime_hint: early warning of soft landing failure
failure_condition: Over 100 triggered events, the 5-day forward return is non-negative in more than 50% of cases (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising home sales (HOUST) above 1,500 units predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days, as housing demand recovery supports consumer confidence and equity valuations.
failure_condition: In high-inflation regimes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly above the 30-day rolling mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 205 for three consecutive months indicates disinflation, which precedes a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as market anticipates rate cut expectations.
failure_condition: Over 100 such triggers, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of cases (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% in the prior month, accompanied by rising wage growth (implied by PAYEMS), triggers a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days as labor market tightness supports equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% AND PAYEMS > 200,000 in the prior month
failure_condition: In high-inflation regimes, the 60-day forward return is not statistically superior to the 30-day rolling average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in retail sales (implied by PAYEMS falling below 120,000 for two months) predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days, reflecting investor concerns about consumer demand weakness.
failure_condition: Over 50 such contractions, the 5-day forward return is not negative in more than 40% of cases (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 200 for 10 consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in employment (PAYEMS), predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as markets anticipate prolonged disinflation and potential rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 200 for 10 consecutive months AND PAYEMS < 220,000 for the same period
failure_condition: In regimes with strong GDP growth, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05).
